intro: Vietnam from top to bottom with private guides. Hanoi's old quarter and water puppets, a night on a cruise boat among Ha Long Bay's limestone islands, the imperial citadel and royal tombs of Hue, the Hai Van Pass to Hoi An's lantern-lit old town and beaches, the energy of Ho Chi Minh City, and a night aboard a wooden rice-barge cruise on the Mekong Delta with its floating markets. The Mekong cruise sails on set days, so we fit your dates to its schedule.
highlights: A water puppet show in Hanoi
Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum, the Temple of Literature and a cyclo ride
An overnight cruise in Ha Long Bay with Surprise Cave
Hue's Imperial Citadel and the tombs of Tu Duc and Khai Dinh

The Hai Van Pass and the Marble Mountains
Hoi An's old town, tailors and beaches
Reunification Palace and Chinatown in Ho Chi Minh City
A night on the Mekong and the Cai Rang floating market

best_time: February to April is good everywhere. The central coast (Hue, Hoi An) has heavy rain and floods from about September to November; the north is cool from December to February.
seasons: Dry and warm across the country.
Hot and humid; afternoon storms in the north and south; good on the central coast.
Typhoons and floods in Hue and Hoi An; Ha Long cruises may be cancelled in storms.
Cool and misty in Hanoi and Ha Long; dry and warm in the south.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

faqs.q: Is there support while we travel?
faqs.a: Yes. You have our 24/7 travel desk on +91 97148 59797 and +91 98242 21400 and a WhatsApp group with your consultant for the whole trip.

good_to_know.title: Hotel deposit
good_to_know.text: Use a credit card for the deposit or pre-authorisation at check-in, never a forex or debit card. Forex cards cannot hold funds, many hotels refuse them, and a credit-card hold is released faster.

good_to_know.title: Dong and cash
good_to_know.text: Prices are in Vietnamese dong. Hotels and big shops take cards; markets, street food and small boats need cash. Count zeros carefully: 100,000 and 10,000 notes look similar.

good_to_know.title: Traffic
good_to_know.text: Motorbikes are everywhere. Cross the road at a slow, steady pace so riders can steer around you; do not stop or run.

good_to_know.title: Temples and the mausoleum
good_to_know.text: Cover shoulders and knees in pagodas and at Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum, where silence is required and no photos are allowed inside.

dining_intro: Vietnam has a long Buddhist vegetarian tradition: look for 'chay' restaurants near pagodas. Hanoi, Hoi An and Ho Chi Minh City also have Indian restaurants. We register your diet with the cruise boats and hotels.
dining_avoid: Fish sauce (nước mắm) goes into almost everything, including dips and many 'vegetable' dishes. Say 'không nước mắm' and ask for the chay menu.
food_card: Tôi ăn chay. Không thịt, không cá, không hải sản, không trứng, không nước mắm. Không hành, không tỏi. Cảm ơn.
We are strict vegetarians (Jain). No meat, fish, seafood or eggs. No onion, garlic, potato, carrot or any root vegetables. No meat or fish stock. Thank you.
